extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students studying differential equations and dynamical systems
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing first- and second-order ODEs by converting to planar systems, using linear algebra (determinant, eigenvalues/eigenvectors) to classify equilibria, construct general solutions, and draw phase portraits and bifurcation diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré map derivative positivity (p'(x0) > 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The derivative of the Poincaré map at x0 is p'(x0) = exp(∫_0^1 (∂f/∂x0)(s, φ(s,x0)) ds), and hence p'(x0) > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute p' by differentiating the flow with respect to initial condition and using separation of variables; conclude p is strictly increasing wherever this exponential formula applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concavity of Poincaré map bounds number of fixed points
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula for p''(x0) (obtained by differentiating again) can show p''(x0) < 0 (concave down) in specific models (e.g., when ∂^2 f/∂x0^2 ≡ −2a), implying the graph of p is concave down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When p is concave down its graph can cross the diagonal y = x at most twice; thus there are at most two fixed points of p, and at most two periodic solutions of period 1. Compute the second derivative from the given f to verify concavity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic solution <=> fixed point of Poincaré map
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed points x0 with p(x0) = x0 correspond to periodic solutions of the original ODE: φ(t + 1, x0) = φ(t, x0) for all t (period 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show a solution is periodic, show its initial condition is a fixed point of the Poincaré return map (or vice versa). Use the flow φ(t,x0) and the Poincaré map p defined by φ(1,x0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter monotonicity implies bifurcation/extinction behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If ∂f/∂h < 0 then slope-field slopes decrease as h increases, implying the Poincaré map decreases with h; there is a unique h* where p has exactly one fixed point, for h > h* there may be no fixed points (e.g., population dies out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate f with respect to the parameter to determine monotone dependence; track how fixed points of p move or disappear with parameter changes to identify bifurcation values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct bifurcation diagrams by fixing one parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: To study a two-parameter family fa,b(x) = ax − x^3 − b, fix a (e.g., a = 1, 0, −1) and use the graph of fa,b to construct the bifurcation diagram in b for that fixed a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot the graph(s) of f_{a,b} as b varies, find equilibria (roots), determine their stability (using phase lines or derivatives), and assemble the equilibria vs parameter plot (bifurcation diagram). Repeat for several fixed a to understand dependence on a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch regions in parameter plane and describe bifurcation boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ab–plane, sketch regions where the differential equation has different numbers of equilibria and sketch the boundaries between these regions; describe using phase lines and graphs of fa,b(x) the bifurcations that occur as parameters cross these boundaries (including behavior at special points like a = b = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the one-parameter bifurcation diagrams for various fixed values to delineate curves in the ab-plane where equilibria are created/annihilated; near these curves use phase-line sketches and local graphs of f to identify saddle-node, pitchfork, or other bifurcations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze small time-periodic forcing and experimental exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: For x' = x − x^3 − b sin(2π t) with small |b|, study existence of periodic solutions and experimentally explore what happens as |b| increases (observe and explain any bifurcations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat small periodic forcing as a perturbation of the autonomous case: look for persistent periodic solutions via Poincaré map or perturbation arguments; use numerical experiments to detect bifurcations as forcing amplitude grows, then explain phenomena qualitatively/rigorously where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: autonomous system and equilibrium point
rubrics_metrics.description: A system is autonomous if the right-hand side does not depend on t (X' = F(X)). A vector X0 with F(X0) = 0 is an equilibrium point, corresponding to the constant solution X(t) ≡ X0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing a system, first check if it's autonomous; compute equilibria by solving F(X) = 0 and then analyze local behavior near these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce second-order ODEs to first-order planar systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Many second-order ODEs can be transformed into 2D systems by introducing y = x' (so X = (x,y) and X' = (y, f(t,x,y))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this reduction to apply planar system techniques (phase plane, linearization, eigenvalues) to second-order problems such as harmonic oscillators or forced systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant determines uniqueness/quantity of equilibria for linear systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For linear autonomous planar system X' = AX the algebraic system AX = 0 has a unique equilibrium (0,0) iff det A ≠ 0; if det A = 0 (and A ≠ 0) there is a straight line of equilibrium points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute det A = ad − bc for A = [[a,b],[c,d]]. Use det ≠ 0 to conclude the origin is the only equilibrium; det = 0 signals infinitely many equilibria along a line (solve the homogeneous linear equations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear independence criterion for planar vectors via determinant
rubrics_metrics.description: Two vectors V = (v1,v2) and W = (w1,w2) are linearly independent iff det [[v1,w1],[v2,w2]] ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this determinant test to check whether two candidate solution vectors form a basis of R^2 (so that any initial condition can be expanded in that basis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvalues via characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Eigenvalues λ of a 2×2 matrix A are the roots of the characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) (a quadratic in λ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form A − λI, compute its determinant to get a quadratic equation in λ, solve for λ (real, repeated, or complex), and handle each case appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute eigenvectors from (A − λI)V = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: For each eigenvalue λ solve the linear homogeneous system (A − λI)V = 0 to obtain the associated eigenvectors (nonzero solutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After finding λ, substitute into A − λI and find a nonzero column (or parametric family) giving the eigenvector(s); eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: General solution for distinct real eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has two distinct real eigenvalues λ1 ≠ λ2 with eigenvectors V1 and V2, then the general solution of X' = AX is X(t) = α e^{λ1 t} V1 + β e^{λ2 t} V2, and this gives the unique solution for any initial condition X(0) = X0 by expanding X0 in the basis {V1,V2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express the initial vector X0 = αV1 + βV2, then form the linear combination of the two eigen-solutions. Use uniqueness (linearity principle and linear system existence/uniqueness) to conclude this is the unique IVP solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of eigen-solutions and stability from eigenvalue signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each eigen-solution X_i(t) = e^{λ_i t} V_i is a straight-line solution along the ray through V_i. If λ_i > 0 the magnitude |X_i(t)| → ∞ as t → ∞; if λ_i < 0 then X_i(t) → 0 as t → ∞; if λ_i = 0 the solution is constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use signs of eigenvalues to decide growth/decay along eigen-directions and to infer local stability properties of the equilibrium at the origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: saddle and phase-portrait description for λ1<0<λ2
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has real eigenvalues with λ1 < 0 < λ2, the origin is a saddle: the eigenvector for λ1 spans the stable line (solutions along it tend to origin as t→∞) and the eigenvector for λ2 spans the unstable line (solutions along it tend away as t→∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot straight-line (eigen) solutions and representative trajectories: general solutions approach the unstable direction as t→∞ and the stable direction as t→−∞. Use this to draw phase portraits and identify stable/unstable manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodicity condition for linear nonautonomous equation x' = p(t) x
rubrics_metrics.description: If p(t) is differentiable and periodic with period T, then all solutions are periodic with period T iff ∫_0^T p(s) ds = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the integrating factor or explicit solution x(t) = x(0) exp(∫_0^t p(s) ds) and check the condition on the integral over one period to verify periodicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a periodic solution from sign-separated bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(t,x) is C^1 and T-periodic in t and there exist constants p < q with f(t,p) > 0 and f(t,q) < 0 for all t, then there exists a T-periodic solution x(t) with p < x(0) < q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use upper/lower solutions and the intermediate-value principle applied to the Poincaré map to show a fixed point exists between p and q, yielding a periodic orbit.
